articles.title: Floating Garden Cuts Pollution from Farm Ponds by Nearly a Third
articles.summary: Scientists in Victoria, Australia have come up with a clever way to help the environment — a floating garden made of native plants placed on top of wastewater ponds. The garden works by absorbing harmful gases that would normally escape into the air. Researchers found that this method reduced greenhouse gas emissions from a wastewater lagoon by around 30 percent. Encouraged by these results, the team is now testing the same idea on farm dams across the country. If it works widely, this low-cost, nature-based solution could help farmers reduce pollution while also supporting local wildlife. It shows that sometimes the best ideas come straight from nature itself.

lv2: Why do you think using native plants is important for this type of environmental project? (你認為為什麼在這類環保項目中使用本地植物很重要？)
How does a floating garden help reduce greenhouse gases from wastewater ponds? (漂浮花園如何幫助減少廢水池塘的溫室氣體排放？)
lv3: Should governments make it compulsory for all farms to use nature-based pollution solutions like floating gardens? Why or why not? (政府是否應該強制要求所有農場採用漂浮花園等以大自然為本的污染解決方案？為什麼？)
Some people argue that technology, not nature, is the best way to fight pollution. Do you agree? What are the strengths and weaknesses of each approach? (有人認為對抗污染最好的方法是科技而非大自然，你同意嗎？兩種方法各有什麼優缺點？)

articles.title: Identical Twins, Different Health: Scientists Investigate Why Our Immune Systems Differ
articles.summary: Have you ever wondered why two people raised in the same home can have very different health experiences? Scientists are studying a pair of identical twins named Nicole and Amanda, who share the exact same DNA but have developed quite different immune systems over their lifetimes. Even though twins like them start out biologically the same, things like diet, stress, sleep, and their surroundings can gradually change how their bodies fight illness. Researchers hope that by comparing the twins closely, they can discover new clues about why some people get sick more often than others — and how we might one day better protect everyone's health.

lv1: What is special about the two twins in this story? (這個故事中的兩名雙胞胎有什麼特別之處？)
What are scientists hoping to learn by studying the twins? (科學家希望透過研究這對雙胞胎了解什麼？)
lv2: Even though identical twins have the same DNA, why might their immune systems become different over time? (即使同卵雙胞胎擁有相同的DNA，為什麼她們的免疫系統會隨時間變得不同？)
Why is it useful for scientists to study twins rather than two unrelated people when researching health differences? (研究健康差異時，科學家為什麼研究雙胞胎比研究兩個無關的人更有用？)
lv3: If scientists discover exactly what causes some people to have stronger immune systems, should this information be used to create personalised medicine for everyone? What ethical issues might arise? (若科學家發現導致某些人擁有更強免疫系統的確切原因，這些資訊是否應用於為每個人創造個人化醫療？可能出現哪些道德問題？)
Does this research suggest that our lifestyle choices matter more than our genes for our health? Use evidence from the article to support your view. (這項研究是否說明生活方式的選擇比基因對健康更重要？請用文章中的證據支持你的觀點。)

articles.title: 東涌公屋混凝土強度不達標　房委會要求建商提交糾正方案
articles.summary: 房屋委員會在例行測試中，發現東涌第42區一個公營房屋項目的部分建築組件所用混凝土強度未能符合標準。事件引起社會對公屋建築質素的關注。房委會已要求負責建設的承建商盡快提交糾正及改善方案，並會繼續監督情況，確保住宅安全。有關工程涉及多個樓層結構，當局表示正深入調查問題成因，以保障未來住戶的安全。此事再次引發外界對本港公共建築監管制度是否足夠嚴謹的討論。

lv1: 房委會在哪個地區的公屋項目發現混凝土強度問題？
房委會要求承建商提交什麼文件？
lv2: 混凝土強度不達標對住宅安全可能造成什麼影響？

lv3: 你認為政府應如何加強監管公共建築工程的質素，以防止類似問題再次發生？

articles.title: PISA排名下滑敲響警鐘　立法限制「數碼分心」成教育新議題
articles.summary: 香港學生在國際學生能力評估計劃（PISA）的排名出現下滑，令教育界和政界人士深感憂慮。有分析指出，學生過度使用智能手機及沉迷社交媒體，導致專注力下降，影響學習表現。有建議提出應透過立法手段，限制學生在校內及學習時間使用數碼設備，以減少「數碼分心」的問題。支持者認為此舉有助提升學習效率，但反對者則擔心過度限制會妨礙學生接觸新科技的機會，雙方各有論據，議題引發社會廣泛討論。

lv1: PISA是什麼？它主要評估學生哪方面的能力？
lv2: 為什麼有人認為過度使用智能手機會影響學生的學習成績？
立法限制學生使用數碼設備有什麼好處和壞處？
lv3: 你認為限制學生在校內使用手機是解決學習問題的最佳方法嗎？還是應該從其他方向入手？請說明理由。
在數碼時代，學校應如何在善用科技與防止數碼分心之間取得平衡？你有什麼具體建議？
